label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 8, samples with blocking 27

A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 27 samples

report.summary: 13% of transfers returned 500 and p95 was 2.1 s. An idle-in-transaction session (28110) blocked ledger_app sessions from 03:23:17 to 03:24:09, which fits the slowdown. Nothing directly links it to the 500s.

findings.claim: Transfers had 86 HTTP 500s out of 662 requests (13%), with p95 2.1 s and p99 3.8 s.
findings.reason: Request metrics are complete and show the error ratio and latency tail.

findings.claim: A session idle in transaction (28110) blocked several ledger_app sessions for up to 1.8 s between 03:23:17 and 03:24:09.
findings.reason: Historical blocker samples show 8 blocked sessions waiting on 28110, which was idle in transaction.

findings.claim: Outbox arrivals dropped (9-17 per 10 s) in the same period as the blocking. The outbox consumer and connection pool are ruled out as the cause.
findings.reason: Delivery attempts took about 71 ms with no errors, and the pool had no pending borrowers or timeouts. The commit slowdown is therefore upstream of both.

limitations: There is no time-bucketed view of the 500s, so they cannot be matched to the 03:23:17-03:24:09 blocking window.
Blocking was sampled every 2 s, and the source of the idle-in-transaction session was not identified. The 296 FAILED outbox rows (about 9.6 hours old) predate the window and are unexplained.
next_checks: Get application error logs, or 500 counts per time bucket, for the transfers route and compare them with 03:23:17-03:24:09.
Identify what session 28110 is (its application and last statement) and why it stays idle in a transaction.

alternatives.reason: No error logs or per-request timeline were collected, so the 500s are not tied to the blocked window.
alternatives.hypothesis: The 500s come from a different cause, such as application errors or constraint failures, unrelated to the blocking.

alternatives.reason: All 577 deliveries succeeded in about 71 ms with no server or network errors.
alternatives.hypothesis: The outbox consumer or delivery path caused the failures.
